subject: Urgent: Dedicated pool saturation impacting Nimbus Retail production
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@nimbusretail.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: SRE Team <sre@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors and latency spike - urgent

Hi Priyom,

We're seeing a sustained latency spike and a rising number of 502/504 errors from our production models since ~08:45 PDT. The errors correlate with longer inference queues and an increase in tail latency for our primary checkout flow. Our SREs captured a representative log excerpt (attached) and a short timeline. This is causing checkout failures for ~2.3% of sessions and is customer-visible.

Can you confirm if this is related to your dedicated GPU pool or something on our side? We urgently need a mitigation path — even temporary routing to a different capacity tier would help while you investigate.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Retail
attachments: nimbus_error_sample.log (text, 24KB)
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alice Park <alice@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike - urgent

Alice — thank you for the quick heads up and the logs. We're seeing the same signal in our telemetry: a spike in queue depth and a drop in per-reservation throughput for Nimbus' reserved capacity. Preliminary indicators point to a saturated dedicated GPU pool serving the reserved instances in this region (us-west-2).

Immediate plan (next 60 minutes):
- Routing: We'll open an emergency overflow route to our hosted pool for your highest-priority route(s) to reduce tail latency — Marcus, can you confirm feasibility and ETA?
- Headroom: Triggering a temporary burst allocation to Nimbus' reserved quota while we root cause.
- Telemetry: Naomi will pull token-level traces and token-backpressure metrics and share a short snapshot.
- Customer comms: I'll coordinate a status note for your execs; please confirm the external contact list.

We view this as high priority — looping in Marcus and Naomi to run triage.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Dedicated & Private accounts
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Alice Park <alice@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike - urgent

Folks — quick technical readout:
- Observed: sustained batch queue growth on nodes assigned to Nimbus' reserved pool beginning ~08:40 PDT. GPU utilization at 98–100% + increasing KV-cache evictions. Per-request latency tail shows P99 jumping from ~220ms -> ~1.4s.
- Root cause hypothesis: workload burst pattern exceeded configured batching windows and the current kernel selection path is triggering slower kernels under long sequences; combined with other tenants' background jobs consuming headroom.

Proposed immediate mitigations (safe, low-risk):
1) Overflow routing: Allow highest-priority route to use hosted fleet (downgrade disabled features temporarily if needed). Estimated cutover 8–15 minutes once network ACLs applied. See attached route_proposal.md.
2) Temporary burst capacity: Grant Nimbus an additional 2 reserved GPU slots from our burst pool for 4 hours — this should reduce queueing by ~60% based on model fingerprints.
3) Autoscaling override: Force-scale dedicated pool by +15% (temp) to relieve node-level hot spots.
4) Longer-term: We'll run a guided quantization/seq-length tuning session for Nimbus to reduce per-token work.

I'll start the overflow flow now and post updates here. Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
attachments: route_proposal.md (text, 3KB)
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Alice Park <alice@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike - urgent

Summary from telemetry (short):
- Token throughput for Nimbus' reservation dropped ~42% across the impacted window.
- Error rate (502/504) increased from baseline 0.1% to 2.3% aligned with queue growth.
- Top contributing models: checkout-llm-v2 (seq avg 512) and rec-ranker-v1.

I've attached a quick KPI snapshot (kpi_snapshot_Aug4.pdf) and pushed a trimmed tracing export to the SUP-9923 ticket.

Customer-facing ask: we should propose the temporary burst + overflow routing as Marcus outlined and offer a one-time SLA credit for the impacted hour window. Marissa, can you own the credit conversation and legal signoff? Priyom, I recommend an exec sync at 13:00 PDT to align on mitigation and next steps.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Reliability
attachments: kpi_snapshot_Aug4.pdf (pdf, 240KB)
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alice Park <alice@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike - urgent

Alice — quick update and actions taken: 
- Overflow routing enabled for your checkout route at 10:20 PDT; we saw queue depth drop and P99 latency improve from 1.4s -> ~300ms within 12 minutes.
- Temporary burst of +2 reserved GPUs applied at 10:30 PDT for 4 hours; monitored utilization now ~72%.
- Autoscaling override applied to the dedicated pool; background jobs flagged and throttled.
- Naomi captured the metrics; Marcus filed SUP-9923 with traces and the route proposal.

Next steps:
- Exec sync at 13:00 PDT today (invite sent) to confirm: permanent capacity increase vs. workload tuning, SLA credit terms, and a joint post-mortem schedule.
- We'll follow up with a technical playbook for Nimbus to reduce sequence length and recommended quantization settings.

Marissa will lead the credit/contract discussion and Naomi will share the PM post-mortem template. We aim to have a remediation plan within 48 hours and a capacity sizing proposal within 72 hours.

Please confirm any additional contacts you want on the 13:00 sync and if you need an immediate customer-facing status note for your retail execs.

Thanks for the quick coordination — we'll keep you updated in this thread.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
